crossDomainInvariants.name: Marketplace checkout atomicity
crossDomainInvariants.invariant: Checkout creates canonical marketplace/seller order, fulfillment/reservation/payment allocation/settlement and idempotency records while applying inventory consequences in one SQLite transaction.
crossDomainInvariants.boundary: Marketplace orchestrates; Inventory and Payment remain canonical authorities.

crossDomainInvariants.name: Marketplace cancellation compensation
crossDomainInvariants.invariant: Cancellation releases reserved stock once and creates canonical Payment refund identity while updating Marketplace projections and lifecycle rows atomically.
crossDomainInvariants.boundary: Marketplace orchestrates; Payment refund and Inventory movement remain canonical.

crossDomainInvariants.name: Payment financial decision and ledger
crossDomainInvariants.invariant: Financial state, evidence/verification binding, ledger entries, idempotency and marketplace settlement consequences are transactionally coordinated.
crossDomainInvariants.boundary: Payment Core remains sole financial decision and ledger authority.

crossDomainInvariants.name: Fulfillment and delivery command lifecycle
crossDomainInvariants.invariant: Commands validate tenant/org/location/courier scope, durable replay, proof/lifecycle transitions and existing Inventory consequences within transaction boundaries.
crossDomainInvariants.boundary: Preserve frozen Order → Fulfillment → Delivery Assignment → Delivery Lifecycle → Proof/Exception → Inventory consequence chain; Payment/Settlement remain outside Logistics.

crossDomainInvariants.name: Procurement receipt and Inventory posting
crossDomainInvariants.invariant: Receipt intent binds to approved procurement-origin PO lines and organization location; receipt and canonical inventory movement posting must remain transactionally coherent and replay-safe.
crossDomainInvariants.boundary: Procurement owns receipt intent; Inventory owns stock movement.

crossDomainInvariants.name: Procurement RFQ-time capacity snapshot
crossDomainInvariants.invariant: Capacity evidence is snapshotted per invited supplier at RFQ creation with capture time; later evidence changes must not rewrite historical RFQ snapshot.
crossDomainInvariants.boundary: Supplier Network owns source evidence; Procurement owns immutable RFQ snapshot. Neither authorizes operational scheduling.

crossDomainInvariants.name: Service resource and booking commitment
crossDomainInvariants.invariant: Booking/resource/availability/commitment state shares resource/location scope and idempotent command records.
crossDomainInvariants.boundary: Service capability owns booking/resource commitments; no second Logistics Scheduling authority.

limitations: Every literal db.prepare/db.exec call is recorded; multi-statement exec blocks and trigger bodies are split into complete SQL statements in sqlite-sql-statements.json.
The enclosing exported function and nearest named function scope are both recorded. Arrow-function/callback indirection can make nearest local function ownership approximate.
SQL table access is derived from syntax; dynamic table names and application-level reads through helper return values need manual review.
Transaction markers are syntactic; caller-owned transactions and helper calls require call-graph verification.
Repeated migration declarations are preserved in declaration lines; deduplicated FK edges are distinct from raw declarations.
Table ownership is provisional and supported by schema and observed DML access; it is not based on names alone.
SQL text is normalized for whitespace and comments; string literals and statement semantics are retained.
No production code or schema was changed; no extraction is approved.
